description: Trust bars, logo strips, certifications and badges, stat rows and guarantees: the quick, checkable reasons a homeowner can let this company into their house. Ranges from a one-line rating + supplier logos under the hero to a full credentials grid or a signed guarantee.
queries: company stats section with key numbers
construction company certifications and awards section

references.layout: Centred light heading on a deep plum band, then a 3×3 grid of cream cards (~200×80, ~2px radius, ~10px gaps). Each card has a badge or logo (~48px) on the left, then a bold title, a one-line description and an underlined 'LEARN MORE →' link.
references.type: Heading geometric sans light ~28px; card titles sans semibold ~12px; descriptions ~10px; link monospace caps ~8px, tracked.
references.color: Band ~#5A0F45 plum; cards ~#F7EEDF cream; card text ~#2A1A22; heading ~#F3DDEA.
details: Every badge gets a one-line plain-English explanation of what it means
Monospace 'LEARN MORE →' links give every credential a way to verify it
Logos keep their own colours but sit on identical cream tiles, so the grid stays calm
A saturated dark band makes this a distinct 'proof' moment on the page
references.why_it_works: Credentials mean nothing if visitors don't know what they are; this pairs each badge with a sentence and a link.
references.trade_adaptation: 'Licensed & insured (Lic. #…)', 'GAF Master Elite', 'NATE-certified technicians', 'EPA Lead-Safe', 'BBB A+', 'Angi Super Service', each with what it means for the homeowner and a link to verify.

references.layout: A tiny dot + 'Awards' label top-left, then full-width rows divided by hairlines. Each row has a large serif statement on the left ('Built In: Best places to work 2023') and a small badge thumbnail (~40px) aligned right.
references.type: Serif ~30px regular, sentence case, written as 'Issuer: achievement'; label ~9px sans.
references.color: Light warm grey ~#EEEDE8 ground; text ~#1B1B1B; hairlines ~#C9C8C2.
details: The 'Issuer: what it means' colon structure makes every line self-explanatory
Badges shrink to thumbnails at the edge, so the text leads and the logos only confirm
Huge type and very few rows (four): confidence through restraint
references.why_it_works: It turns a pile of mismatched badges into a typographic list, and it still works when the badge artwork is ugly.
references.trade_adaptation: 'Owens Corning: Platinum Preferred Contractor', 'State of Ohio: Master Plumber #12345', 'Angi: Super Service Award 2024', 'Family-owned: since 1987'. Ideal for premium and editorial styles.

references.layout: Full-bleed saturated band. Stats stack vertically as giant rows ('20 Years', '300+ Employees', '02 Offices'), each spanning ~70% of the width, with a short paragraph (~9px) in the right column. Hairlines divide the rows, and lower rows fade in opacity.
references.type: Transitional serif ~72px light/regular, with number and noun on one line at the same size; supporting copy small sans ~9px.
references.color: Electric blue ~#2B3FE8 ground; type ~#F2F2F2 fading to ~#8C97F0; dividers ~rgba(255,255,255,0.15).
details: Number and noun are set together as one phrase ('20 Years') instead of a number over a label
A leading zero ('02 Offices') keeps the typographic rhythm
Each stat gets a short sentence explaining it
The progressive fade suggests rows revealing on scroll
references.why_it_works: It makes three plain facts feel monumental, and it is far more memorable than a row of four small counters.
references.trade_adaptation: '38 Years', '4,200 Roofs', '1 Family', with one sentence each, on a band in the brand colour. Suits a bold or premium roofer or electrician.

references.layout: One large rounded card (~24px radius, soft shadow) split in two. Left: a bold graphic (a thick orange quarter-ring) at the top, three small round badges, the heading, a two-line guarantee with the promise in bold, and a handwritten signature in white at the bottom. Right: four stacked dark tiles, each with a tiny icon, a bold title and a grey one-liner.
references.type: Heading sans ~22px regular; guarantee sentence ~9px with a bold lead-in; tile titles ~10px semibold; signature as a script image.
details: The guarantee is specific and measurable: 'Paid First Sprint, 100% refund if we miss'
The founder's signature sits under the promise, making someone personally accountable
Risk-reducers are split into four short tiles
One bold geometric shape does all the decorating
references.why_it_works: A guarantee only persuades when it is specific and someone signs it, and this does both in one compact, striking card.
references.trade_adaptation: 'If it leaks within 10 years, we fix it free.' signed by the owner; tiles: 'Upfront flat-rate pricing', 'Clean-up included', 'Licensed & insured', 'On time or $50 off'.

references.layout: Full-width centred band: a circular seal (~80px) drawn as a progress-ring arc reading '30 DAY · MONEY-BACK GUARANTEE', a serif headline, a three-line explanation and an outlined pill button.
references.type: Seal number serif ~28px; seal label tiny caps, tracked; headline serif ~22px; body sans ~11px.
references.color: Plum ~#6E1B4F band; white text; seal ring white with a gradient fade; button outlined white.
details: The seal is a ring arc, not a gold clip-art medallion
Plain-language terms sit right under the headline ('contact Support within 30 days and get a full refund')
Only one call to action
references.why_it_works: A self-contained, centred promise band with a custom seal is quick to scan and doesn't look like clip art.
references.trade_adaptation: A '10 YEAR WORKMANSHIP WARRANTY' or '100% SATISFACTION' seal drawn in CSS, the terms in one sentence, and a 'Book your free estimate' button.

references.layout: Left-aligned serif headline, then four equal columns, each with a thin line icon (~20px), a 2-3 line bold claim (~14px) and a small 'Learn more ↗' link.
references.type: Headline transitional serif ~36px regular; claims sans ~14px semibold; links ~9px.
references.color: White ground; black ~#111111 text and icons.
details: The headline is human ('A little peace of mind'), not 'Why choose us'
Claims are concrete ('No surprise fees or long-term contracts required')
Line icons are drawn in the text colour, not inside colourful circles
references.why_it_works: It is the cleanest way to state three or four assurances, and the serif headline with monochrome line icons keeps it premium.
references.trade_adaptation: 'No surprise fees', 'Licensed, bonded & insured', '2-year labor warranty', 'We clean up after ourselves', each linking to details.

references.layout: One slim row (~40px tall): 'G2 ★★★★★ 2,000+ reviews →' in grey on the left, six customer logos evenly spaced on the right.
references.color: White ground; text and stars grey ~#6B6B6B; logos mostly monochrome ~#1A1A1A, with faint native colour kept on a couple.
details: Rating and logos share one line under the hero, costing almost no vertical space
Stars are grey, not yellow
The arrow makes the rating a link
references.why_it_works: It is the most efficient trust bar: one line carrying two kinds of proof.
references.trade_adaptation: '★ 4.9 · 300+ Google reviews →' on the left, manufacturer and supplier logos (Carrier, Trane, Kohler, Sherwin-Williams) in monochrome on the right, directly under the hero.

references.layout: A centred italic caption above a single edge-to-edge row of ~9 small, evenly spaced logos.
references.color: Dark chocolate ~#2A140C ground; logos and caption tinted warm taupe ~#9C8577 at reduced opacity.
details: Every logo is recoloured to one warm taupe, because brand-coloured logos would fight the palette
Italic serif caption 'Trusted by teams at leading companies': soft, not shouty
Dark warm brown instead of black
references.why_it_works: It shows how to make a logo strip feel premium: one monochrome tint matched to the palette, a tiny caption and plenty of air.
references.trade_adaptation: For a premium remodeler or landscaper: supplier and partner logos (Marvin, Andersen, Belgard, Trex) recoloured to a warm tint on a deep brown band, captioned 'Materials we trust' in italic serif.

references.layout: A centred stack in three tiers: two compliance badges side by side with a one-line caption; a central rating emblem (logo, big stars, '4.8/5') flanked on each side by two short quotes with their own star rows; a row of five award shields.
references.type: Captions sans ~10px; flanking quotes ~10px in curly quotes; score ~10px.
references.color: White ground; platform red-orange ~#FF492C for the stars and emblem; text ~#333333.
details: Two-to-four-word quotes ('Game-changing.') flank the rating like laurel leaves
The compliance badges get one explanatory sentence
All three tiers of proof sit symmetrically on one centre axis
references.why_it_works: A compact composition that combines certifications, a rating and review snippets without a single box.
references.trade_adaptation: Top: 'Licensed · Insured' badges with 'Lic. #12345 · $2M liability'. Centre: Google 4.9 flanked by four two-word snippets ('Spotless work.', 'On time.'). Bottom: manufacturer certifications.

references.layout: A single wide white card (~460×120, ~28px radius, large soft shadow), centred. Two platform ratings sit side by side with a thin divider between them (logo on top; score + stars, or score + bar, below). A rotated green starburst sticker reading 'TOP RATED' overlaps the top-left corner.
references.type: Logos ~24px; scores ~14px grey; sticker caps ~9px white bold, rotated ~-20°.
references.color: White card on a white page with a ~rgba(0,0,0,0.08) shadow; sticker ~#5DAE7B; native platform colours (green ~#0CAA41, purple bar ~#7C3AED).
details: A starburst sticker slapped on the corner at an angle: playful and hand-applied
The second metric is a progress bar instead of stars, for variety
A very large radius plus shadow makes the card feel like an object
references.why_it_works: It turns two numbers into a memorable object, and the sticker adds personality without clutter.
references.trade_adaptation: Google 4.9 ★ next to 'BBB A+' or 'Nextdoor Neighborhood Fave' in one big card with a 'LOCAL FAVORITE' or 'SINCE 1987' sticker. Fits friendly and playful styles (cleaners, pest control).

references.layout: A wide team photo with a 4-column stat table attached directly beneath it: the top row of cells holds big numbers and the bottom row holds labels, all cells bordered with 1px yellow lines. Below, a separate yellow band reads 'Our Investors' with logos.
references.type: Numbers rounded heavy grotesk ~26px; labels sans ~11px; sub-labels ~8px.
references.color: Cream ~#FBF7EC ground; borders and band ~#FFC800 yellow; numbers aubergine ~#3B0A2C.
details: The stats are physically attached to the team photo, like a caption table
One joke stat ('25k Gummy bears eaten') adds personality
A sub-label carries detail ('Porto & Berlin' under 'Offices')
references.why_it_works: It grounds the numbers in a real photo of the people behind them and uses a table grid instead of floating counters.
references.trade_adaptation: Crew photo with a table underneath: '1987 Founded', '3 Trucks', '4,100 Jobs', '∞ Pots of coffee'. Great for friendly and rustic styles.

references.layout: Italic serif 'Awards' label top-left; to its right, a grid of beige tiles (~110×60, ~6px radius, three per row), each holding one award logo recoloured to a single muted brown.
references.type: Label italic serif ~22px; logos keep their own lettering but are flattened to one colour.
details: Every badge is flattened to one muted colour, so wildly different logos look like a set
Uniform tiles give each badge equal weight
Label on the left, grid on the right: an asymmetric layout
references.why_it_works: It shows the key trick for trade badges, whose manufacturer artwork is often garish: flatten them to one colour on matching tiles.
references.trade_adaptation: GAF, CertainTeed, BBB, Angi and HomeAdvisor badges flattened to the brand's ink colour on paper-tone tiles.

takeaways: Explain every credential: pair each badge with a plain sentence about what it means (license number, coverage, what the certification requires) and, ideally, a link to verify it.
Flatten logos and badges to one tint that matches the palette; uniform tiles make mismatched artwork read as a set.
Fewer, bigger facts beat many small counters. '38 Years' set as one phrase beats '38+' over 'Years in business'.
Make guarantees specific and measurable, and have a named person sign them.
Put the cheapest trust (a one-line rating + monochrome logos) directly under the hero. Save the full credentials grid for lower on the page or the About page.
Ground stats in a real crew, truck or shop photo where possible.
One playful device (a sticker, a joke stat) adds personality; stacking several cheapens it.
avoid: Rows of colourful G2-style award shields (monday.com, ClickUp, Apollo): noisy and generic
Stats with a clip-art icon above each number (Deel)
Bright-blue stat cards reading '100,000+' with carousel arrows
'Trusted by 10,000+ customers' logo walls of big brands that a local trade wouldn't plausibly serve
Vague guarantees ('Quality guaranteed!') on a gold-ribbon clip-art seal
Percentage stats with no source or date
Dark glassmorphism tiles with 99.99% SLA-style numbers, which read as dev tooling
